headline: Local Film Enthusiast Demands 'Letter of Appreciation' from Anyone He Vaguely Recalls Seeing in a Movie Once
body:
Vikram Sethi, a 34-year-old account manager who claims to have watched ‘Delhi Belly’ during his college years, has begun mailing formal certificates of endorsement to every person he spots in public who reminds him of a character from a movie. Sethi’s new project involves tracking down total strangers, approaching them with a laminated document, and insisting they accept his public validation regardless of their personal connection to the film industry.

“It’s about moral support,” said Sethi, who spent his entire Sunday morning chasing a delivery driver through a crowded mall because the man’s mustache ‘perfectly captured the spirit of mid-2000s indie cinema.’ “Whether it’s a director, a lead actor, or a guy who just looks like he should be in a screenplay, they deserve to know that I am rooting for them from my living room couch. It is a fundamental duty of the audience to issue these letters whenever the global narrative gets complicated.”

Legal experts remain confused by the initiative, noting that Sethi has no actual authority to issue endorsements, nor does he know any of the individuals he is currently ‘backing.’ Undeterred, Sethi has expanded his operations to include local grocery store clerks, whom he has officially notified that he finds their stock-management style 'incredibly authentic and underrated' in the current market climate.
caption: Next time you see a stranger, do you also feel the urge to send them a formal certificate of appreciation for their general existence? #Cinema #Fans #UnsolicitedValidation #DelhiBelly (satire)
igHook: Would you accept a formal letter of praise from a total stranger if they thought you looked like a movie character?
